impact:
`src/format.ts` computes padding as `width - s.length`. CPython's `f"{s:<width>}"` pads on `len(s)`, which counts code points. Any non-BMP character in a display string therefore gets one space too few per astral char, misaligning the whole column.

Measured: `padRight("<rocket>a", 5)` emits 3 spaces in the port, 4 in Python.

LATENT TODAY: no renderer or CLI exists in `src/` yet and nothing imports these helpers — T-004 is what wires them up. It becomes reachable the moment tables render, and the trigger is user-controlled: the config `renames` map takes arbitrary strings, and encoded project names derive from real paths.

Note this is the same root cause as the encodePath issue (JS counting UTF-16 units where Python counts code points) but a separate site and a separate fix, so it is filed separately.

Caveat worth recording: correct display width is not simply code-point count either — CPython's format spec pads on `len()`, so matching Python byte-for-byte means counting code points, NOT grapheme clusters and NOT East-Asian display width. Matching Python is the contract; do not "improve" on it.

FIX: count code points (`[...s].length` or `Array.from(s).length`), and add a CPython differential test over astral, combining-mark, and wide-CJK inputs so T-004's table layout is pinned before the renderers land.

title: padRight/padLeft pad by UTF-16 code units while claiming CPython format-spec semantics
